title: Bug: [memory_checker] Failed to get container ID of <name> during config reload
author: rajkumar1-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

Memory-checker fails with `Failed to get container ID of <name>` during config reload, that is being caught by loganalyzer that causes multiple tests failure

### Steps to Reproduce

Flakey in nature
do a config reload and memory checker will occasionally emit the  error log to syslog: `2026 Jun 28 09:28:35.485290 bjw-can-7260-14 ERR memory_checker: [memory_checker] Failed to get container ID of 'gnmi'! Exiting ...`

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual Behavior: memory-checker is exiting with non-zero code
Expected Behavior: config reload case should be handled



### Relevant log output

```shell
>               pt_assert(False, failure_message)
E               Failed: Got matched syslog in processes "analyze_logs--<MultiAsicSonicHost bjw-can-7260-14>" exit code:"1"
E               match: 1
E               expected_match: 0
E               expected_missing_match: 0
E               
E               Match Messages:
E               2026 Jun 28 09:28:35.485290 bjw-can-7260-14 ERR memory_checker: [memory_checker] Failed to get container ID of 'gnmi'! Exiting ...
```

linkedPullRequests.author: rajkumar1-arista
linkedPullRequests.body:
Fix memory_checker false alarms during config reload

Fixes: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/26428

<!--
     Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines:
     https://github.com/Azure/SONiC/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md

     If this is a bug fix, make sure your description includes "fixes #xxxx", or
     "closes #xxxx" or "resolves #xxxx"

     Please provide the following information:
-->

#### Why I did it
During config reload, Monit continues to invoke `memory_checker` for individual containers (`container_memory_gnmi`, `container_memory_snmp`, etc.) while those containers are being stopped and restarted. This causes `memory_checker` to log syslog errors like "`Failed to get container ID of 'gnmi'`" which LogAnalyzer catches.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**: 38614044

#### How I did it
 Two fixes:

1. [sonic-utilities]\[ https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-utilities/pull/4710 \]: Unmonitor container_memory_* checks during service restart. Add `_get_monit_services_by_prefix()` to discover `container_memory_*` services from monit summary, and unmonitor/monitor them in `_stop_services()`/`_restart_services()`.

2. [memory_checker][this]: Re-check container state before logging errors. If memory_checker was already running when config reload starts, the unmonitor only prevents future invocations. Add `exit_if_container_stopped()` to re-check whether the container is still running before logging error. If it stopped, exit gracefully.

comments.author: StormLiangMS
comments.body:
@rajkumar1-arista Review update from 202605 failure triage:

The PR is aligned with the active `memory_checker` false-alarm failures seen on 7260 T1 `test_pfcwd_show_stat`, and the CI checks look green. I found one functional gap that can still leave the `cgroup memory usage file ... does not exist` signature unfixed:

`exit_if_container_stopped(container_name)` only checks whether a container with the same name is currently running. If `memory_checker` already captured the old container ID, then config reload stops and quickly recreates the same container name with a new ID, the old cgroup file can disappear while `container_name` is present again. In that case the current code will still log the same ERR-level `cgroup memory usage file ... does not exist` false alarm.

Could you please make the guard compare the original `container_id` with the current container ID for `container_name` (or otherwise detect that the original container disappeared/restarted), and add a unit test for: old cgroup file missing, same container name running again with a different ID => exit 0/no ERR?

Also, for the 202605 cherry-pick request, the PR body still needs the explicit tracking issue/work item and failure type filled in, plus target-branch test evidence/image version as requested by the bot. The relevant public issue is sonic-mgmt#26428 and ADO is 38614044.

comments.author: StormLiangMS
comments.body:
@rajkumar1-arista Thanks for the update. The new `container_id` comparison covers the specific "same container name, new ID" case I called out earlier, and the PR body now has the 202605 tracking/test evidence.

I found two remaining race/regression issues in the latest patch:

1. Please restore `ignore_removed=True` in `get_running_container_names()`. The current second commit changes:

```python
running_container_list = docker_client.containers.list(filters={"status": "running"})
```

but master currently has `ignore_removed=True`, which was intentionally added by sonic-buildimage#27991 to avoid transient dockerd 404s when a container is removed between Docker's list and inspect operations. Removing it can reintroduce the exact kind of false ERR syslog this PR is trying to eliminate.

2. `_try_get_container_id()` returns `None` for `docker.errors.NotFound`, but `exit_if_container_stopped()` only exits gracefully when `current_id` is truthy and different:

```python
current_id = _try_get_container_id(container_name)
if current_id and current_id != container_id:
    sys.exit(CONTAINER_NOT_RUNNING)
```

If `get_running_container_names()` sees `gnmi`, then the container disappears before `_try_get_container_id('gnmi')`, `current_id` becomes `None` and the code falls through to the original ERR log. That still leaves a config-reload race uncovered. Please treat `NotFound` / `None` as stopped/restarted for this guard, while not silently converting unrelated Docker API failures into a benign result.

Suggested tests: keep/cover `ignore_removed=True`, and add a test where `get_running_container_names()` returns `['gnmi']` but `_try_get_container_id()` returns `None` for the captured old ID; expected result should be exit 0/no ERR.

comments.author: augusdn
comments.body:
Hi @rajkumar1-arista — we tracked a regression in our nightly runs back to this PR, and I wanted to raise it with you directly. Full write-up in #4774.

Short version: after any `config reload`, the `container_memory_*` monit checks are left `Not monitored`. Monitoring for gnmi, snmp, otel, bmp and profiler stays off until something re-monitors them or the box reboots, so the guard that restarts a container over its memory threshold no longer runs.

Here is monit's own log from a single `config reload` on a KVM t0 device:

```
01:07:01.670  monit: 'routeCheck' monitor on user request
01:07:01.698  monit: 'container_checker' monitor on user request
01:07:01.736  monit: 'routeCheck' monitor action done
01:07:01.753  monit: 'container_checker' monitor action done
01:07:01.753  monit: 'container_memory_telemetry' monitor action done
01:07:01.781  monit: 'container_memory_snmp' monitor on user request
01:07:01.809  monit: 'container_memory_profiler' monitor on user request
01:07:01.831  monit: 'container_memory_otel' monitor on user request
01:07:01.856  monit: 'container_memory_gnmi' monitor on user request
01:07:01.908  monit: 'container_memory_bmp' monitor on user request
01:07:01.911  config: Waiting for monit monitor actions to complete ...
01:07:01.982  monit: Reinitializing monit daemon
```

`routeCheck` and `container_checker` each get a `monitor on user request` followed by a matching `monitor action done`. The five services requested after `telemetry` get the request and never a matching `done` — the `monit reload` reinitialises the daemon 71 ms after the last request and the pending actions are discarded. They stay in the state `_stop_services()` left them in, and monit persists that across restarts.

Right after that one reload:

```
Program 'container_memory_gnmi'
  status            Not monitored
  monitoring status Not monitored
```

I think it comes down to an asymmetry in `_restart_services()`: `routeCheck` and `container_checker` are each followed by `_wait_for_monit_service_monitored()`, but the `container_memory_*` loop has no wait and the unconditional `monit reload` follows immediately. The two services that are waited for are exactly the two that survive — which lines up with your helper's docstring noting that `monit monitor <service>` is asynchronous and returns before the action completes.

The fix looks like a few lines — collect the list once and wait for each entry before the reload, the same as the other two. Suggested diff is in the issue.

On why we're confident it's this change rather than something nearby: `_stop_services()` here is the only code in sonic-utilities or sonic-buildimage that issues `monit unmonitor container_memory_*`, so before this PR the state wasn't reachable. On official master builds, `1185710-b7d756b1f` was clean at 0/59 and the first build carrying the submodule bump went to 26/79, with test code unchanged. I also checked the sonic-buildimage half of the feature — `exit_if_container_stopped()` only logs and exits 0, so it isn't involved.

Scope: master and internal images only. The release branches (202505, 202511, 202605) don't have this change and show none of these failures.

Happy to test a patch — we have a reproduction that hits it on the first `config reload`, on both KVM and physical testbeds.

Thanks for taking a look.
